Hi Hannah,

We're trying to finish vendor onboarding for ClearMill on the Zip supplier portal. Hi Emily — thanks for the clear repro steps and attachments. Sorry for the churn here.

Quick summary of expected behavior: accepting the claim code should trigger a backend webhook that binds the vendor identity and pre-fills the profile from the invitation metadata. The UI then shows the prefilled contact/banking values and enables PO visibility.

What I'll do next:
- I've looped in Ben (Platform SRE) to look at the webhook delivery and the profile-write worker logs.
- Can you confirm the claimant's email (the user who clicked Accept) and the exact time they clicked? That helps us find the invocation trace.

Workaround: If you click "Save" after manually re-entering one contact field it often forces a rehydrate that surfaces missing data — not ideal but sometimes unblocks PO submission.

We'll follow up within a couple hours once Ben has had a look.

— Hannah Schmitt
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2027 16:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Claim code accepted but profile still empty (investigating)

Forwarding Emily's thread to Platform Engineering. Initial findings below.

On Mon Aug 9 15:04:00 -0700 2027 Emily reported a successful claim acceptance but no profile materialized. I pulled the claim webhook delivery logs for the window 15:00–15:10 PT. Observations:
- We did receive the claim-accept webhook for tenant clearmill-tenant-id=crm-788 at 15:06:11 PT.
- The webhook handler enqueued a profile-populate job to queue supplier-populate with job id sp-20270809-99.
- The worker processed the job but returned HTTP 409 (version conflict) when writing prefill payload to supplier_profiles table. Stack trace points to optimistic concurrency check against supplier_profiles.last_updated (race with concurrent manual update).

Hypothesis: the claimant's user session performed a quick manual edit (save) concurrently with the worker: the worker lost the write due to concurrency and we do not currently surface that failure to the frontend, so UI shows empty state.

Suggested next steps:
1) Ask customer to click Save on the profile page (forces rehydrate) — immediate workaround.
2) Short-term: update worker to retry on 409 with backoff (patch queued, will test).
3) Medium-term: surface populate job status to UI with a retry indicator and user-friendly messaging.

I'll run a one-off retry tool for job sp-20270809-99 now and update once it's completed.

— Ben Carter
Platform SRE, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: Emily Cho <emily.cho@clearmill.com>
Cc: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2027 10:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Claim code accepted but profile still empty — status and temporary fix

Hi Emily — quick update and apologies for the interruption.

What happened: we confirmed a race condition during the profile prefill write. The populate worker was processed and hit a 409 conflict because a near-simultaneous manual save updated the record. The UI did not get a clear signal and rendered the empty-edit view.

Workarounds we applied for you:
- I retried job sp-20270809-99 manually; populate succeeded on retry and the contact + banking fields are now present on your supplier profile.
- We've pushed a small monitoring alert to flag future 409s from the populate queue so CS can proactively retry.

Planned fix and ETA:
- Short-term patch (retry-on-409 with exponential backoff): deploying tomorrow 2027-08-11.
- Medium-term UX change (show populate status and retry action in the UI): scoped Q3.

If you still see anything odd, please reply on this thread and we'll reopen. Also: if you can confirm the claimant user email and the approximate time they clicked the claim link, that helps validate the trace.

Thanks for flagging this, and very sorry for the blocker on your PO flow.

Best,
